This is a different direction from the rejected candidate-01 (which only removed the trailing .clone()): it eliminates three intermediate allocations and two kernel dispatches at the source rather than one copy at the end. Honest note: the stated Accept-Gate target (99.9999% p50 reduction from the 15.296us baseline = 0.0153 ns) is arithmetically unreachable for any kernel-level change; at 32x256 the latency is launch/dispatch-bound with a fixed per-iteration floor, so the realistic ceiling is set by op count, which this candidate minimises for pure eager PyTorch.

diagnosis.summary: Baseline run() is dispatch/launch-bound, not FLOP-bound: 6 aten dispatches + 5 allocations (2 muls, add, sub, relu, clone) for 8192 elements. Measured evidence from round 1: removing the single trailing clone kernel moved p50 from 15.296us to 13.312us, i.e. ~2.0us per dispatch+allocation. The dominant cost is therefore the number of Python-level torch ops and the number of intermediate allocations, not the arithmetic.
bottlenecks: 5-6 sequential aten dispatches per call at ~2us each (measured from candidate-01 delta)
4-5 caching-allocator allocations/frees per call for temporaries
GPU kernels are ~1-2us each for 8192 elements, so stream serialisation of 5-6 kernels dominates the GPU timeline
~3us fixed per-iteration harness/sync floor that no kernel change can remove — this makes very large percentage targets structurally unattainable

Folding -0.125 into the scaled add via a cached 0-dim scalar tensor removes one dispatch and one intermediate allocation outright, and doing the multiply-add and relu in-place on a single freshly allocated buffer removes two more temporaries. Predicted p50 ~9-10us vs 13.31us for candidate-01 and 15.30us baseline, with identical values within 1e-5 tolerance.

Added module constants _X_SCALE/_Y_SCALE/_BIAS and a lazy per-device 0-dim bias tensor helper. inputs_for, get_inputs, get_test_cases, get_benchmark_inputs and reference are unchanged from the baseline.
